note: Every moment in the game that needs a line. voice: table (the player talking at the table), character (the character speaking in the story), npc (the DM voicing an NPC). fill: the {placeholders} a line may use. split: lines are written separately for each value. needs: extra fields every line must have.

triggers.when: Sitting down at the start of game night, before any dice.
A new scene starts and it is exactly their kind of scene (their archetype loves this scene type).
A new scene starts and it is NOT their kind of scene. Mild grumbling, never mean.
In a social scene, their character opens their mouth first to the NPC.
The session ends. Packing up dice, saying goodnight.
Two characters bicker or joke in character during a scene. The line is spoken to another character (to) and gets a short reply in that character's voice (reply).
Their character just succeeded at a skill check (sneaking, persuading, studying, climbing).
Their character just failed a skill check. Shrugging it off, not despair.
They rolled a natural 20. Big reaction at the table.
They rolled a natural 1. A laugh or a groan, never real anger.
Another player ({other}, playing {other_char}) just pulled something off. Cheering them on.
Another player ({other}, playing {other_char}) just flubbed a roll. Sympathy or teasing.
The boss of the fight ({boss}) shows up. First reaction.
The start of their character's turn in a fight: what they're about to do.
Their character lands an ordinary hit on {target}.
They deal a lot of damage in one turn. Bragging about the number.
Every attack they made this turn missed.
They just took down an enemy ({target}).
Their character casts a spell in a fight.
Oswin heals someone in a fight.
Their character takes a big hit (a third of their hit points or more) but stays up.
Their character drops to 0 hit points.
Another character ({other_char}, played by {other}) just dropped to 0 hit points.
Their character is back on their feet after being down.
Someone just healed or saved their character.
Table chatter between rounds of a fight: initiative, moving minis, rules, snacks.
The party wins the fight.
The party wins, but it was close: someone went down or is nearly out.
The party loses or has to fall back.
Small talk about snacks and drinks between beats.
They are losing interest in the current scene. A small, honest tell, not rude.
They've been on their phone and just looked up. Slightly sheepish.
The DM ruled a roll generously in their favor.
The DM ruled a roll harshly: things got worse.
The DM rolls a big moment in the open, where everyone can see the die.
Under their breath: the DM's hidden rolls have been suspiciously convenient.
Out loud: they ask to see the DM's hidden roll. The table goes quiet. Firm but friendly.
A rules question comes up mid-fight and they have an opinion.
The DM puts them on the spot and they'd rather not be. Awkward, short.
Said right after the session, for the report card. Tier: loved, fun, fine, bored, out.
The NPC's first words when the party meets them in a scene.
The party just handled something well in front of the NPC.
The party just fumbled something in front of the NPC.
The NPC taunts the party mid-fight.
The NPC is beaten in a fight. Last words, played for fun (nobody dies on screen).
The DM announces the party levels up, right there at the table.
Level 3: announcing they've picked Champion for their character (crits on a 19 or 20, an athlete's edge). In their own words, why it's them.
Level 3: announcing they've picked Banner Captain for their character (calls orders so allies get extra attacks, and shields the people beside him). In their own words, why it's them.
Level 3: announcing they've picked Spellguard for their character (a fighter who learns wizard cantrips and turns a hit into a miss). In their own words, why it's them.
Level 3: announcing they've picked Thief for their character (fast hands, climbing and jumping). In their own words, why it's them.
Level 3: announcing they've picked Silvertongue for their character (expertise in talking, and feints that set up her attacks). In their own words, why it's them.
Level 3: announcing they've picked Ambusher for their character (acts first and hits hardest on the first turn). In their own words, why it's them.
Level 3: announcing they've picked Life Domain for their character (stronger heals and a burst of healing for everyone). In their own words, why it's them.
Level 3: announcing they've picked Hearth Domain for their character (temporary hit points for friends and courage against fear). In their own words, why it's them.
Level 3: announcing they've picked Mischief Domain for their character (illusions and a decoy double that draws attacks). In their own words, why it's them.
Level 3: announcing they've picked Evoker for their character (damage spells, and cantrips that still hurt when they miss). In their own words, why it's them.
Level 3: announcing they've picked Wayfinder for their character (teleporting with a friend and moving the party before a fight). In their own words, why it's them.
Level 3: announcing they've picked Mirror Mage for their character (illusions, mirror images and making attackers miss). In their own words, why it's them.

Talk as the NPC (M8, B8): a hero walks up to this person and the DM speaks for them. mood: warm (open, glad to see them), guarded (careful, wants them gone), lie (an easy, innocent face over something they're hiding).
Talk as the NPC (M8, B8): the hero asks about what they came for. warm: they're about to tell what they know (the game then gives the clue). guarded: they won't say. lie: a smooth, false answer.

The hero answers the NPC the DM is voicing (M8, B8), in character. mood: warm (they told you), guarded (they wouldn't), lie_caught (you see through their lie), lie_believed (you take the lie at face value).
